On each observed-content.content-atom write whose source_ref is the telegram source, dispatch ai-records-producer's OWN action:run-ai-records-production DIRECTLY CROSS-SLOT via trigger-engine -> slot::workflow (the PROVEN operator dispatch shape; the old reply-grounded/reply-producer compute.process wrapper stalled on a 5x30s history read before the produce dispatch and never fired on the busy Fly lane, and an external HTTP execute_definition POST is unreliable under lane load — only the trigger->slot::workflow path is reliable). instruction_text=atom.text, output_kind=message, target_group_ref=atom.thread_ref (chat id rides on the result). request_id=atom.id so the reply-poll backstop (same request_id) is idempotent. Producer owns the AI turn; content-distribution owns the consent-gated send (send-poll -> send-reply -> run-publish-intent). No god package, no god-script. payload.justification: Operator decision board record (identity = per-decision hash). Net-new decisions accumulate unbounded (14-48GB); boot-reclaim already bounds status-churn overwrites. decided_at is a real ISO ts, id===address, and agent-decision is NOT an idempotency gate (sweep-cursor + action-intent-receipt drive that) → expiring(30d) bounds the net-new accumulation while keeping a month of decisions for the board.
Receipt is a current-item state machine per identity; only the current version matters. Drop superseded status re-writes — the O(N^2) status-churn source (15-32GB).
Per-tick grounding audit marker (provable by readback, then ephemeral). Reclaim after 7 days.

The canonical single-copy artifact store (WS3b-T4 artifact-once-by-hash). This IS the one true copy every wrapper references; keep the current version. Duplicate mass now lives here once instead of 4x inline.

Grounding INPUT, not exhaust, despite living on an exhaust list-path. produce-grounded.mjs:184-201 reads these by corpus_ref to supply the cite-or-reject excerpts, and its own comment at :188 records what absence costs: reading a path that yielded no slices produced ZERO corpus excerpts and silently ungrounded production, with no error. Deleting a slice therefore degrades output quality invisibly, which is the failure mode retention classes exist to avoid choosing by accident. Durable rather than re-derivable because re-derivable requires a basis_ref_field naming an owner that can rebuild the slice, and no such re-derivation owner was found; corpus_ref identifies the corpus a slice BELONGS to, not a basis it can be regenerated from, so declaring it as one would promise a recovery path that does not exist. Durable rather than expiring because these slices have no natural expiry: a corpus stays valid grounding for as long as its subject does. The owning package knowledge-records was retired in 237bf11f2 and the KIND outlived it, still read by two live processes here, declared as corpus_kind at things-to-store-and-run.json:2086, and explicitly excluded by not_equals filters in current-summary and permission-lease. This policy places the orphaned kind with the package that actually reads it. If the growth this kind was convicted for becomes the binding problem, the correct next move is a re-derivation owner plus a re-derivable policy, never an expiry on grounding input.

payload.name: send-reply (engine-native reply SEND stage)
payload.description: compute.process spawning send-reply.mjs: reads ai-records-producer.result(request_id)->target_group_ref + items[0].text, then FIRE-AND-FORGETS content-distribution action:submit-message-egress. Second half of the produce/send split; content-distribution owns the send (no god package). It dispatches the FRONT DOOR, not the transport: submit-message-egress folds the durable egress-intent record, the fail-closed per-recipient consent gate, the destination lookup by destination_id, and the create-only CAS claim that makes a double-send structurally impossible. It previously dispatched action:run-publish-intent directly, which is the transport SSOT and deliberately carries NO consent gate, so replies to a real person skipped consent. The reply channel is DATA: destination_id and channel are inputs, so a reply on gmail, the Trillion mobile chat, whatsapp or anything added later is a different DATA value and never an edit to this action or its script. Neither is defaulted, because a defaulted channel sends a private reply to the wrong place.

payload.name: send-reply-on-chat-reply-result
payload.description: On each completed ai-records-producer.result whose output_kind is message (the conversational-reply kind, raw assistant text special-cased in the producer), dispatch action:autonomous-agent-tick:send-reply(request_id, destination_id, channel) cross-slot -> slot::workflow. Recipient rides on the result itself (target_group_ref), so there is no side-channel mapping record. THE REPLY ROUTE LIVES HERE, IN DATA, and this is the only place in the package that names a channel: the send script and the action both take it as an input and name none. That is consistent rather than a leak, because the INGEST trigger this pairs with is itself channel-scoped (it matches source_ref == source:telegram), so a channel-scoped trigger carrying its own matching channel is the same fact stated once. Replying on gmail, the Trillion mobile chat, whatsapp or discord is therefore a NEW TRIGGER ROW with a different source_ref match and a different destination_id/channel, never an edit to any code. The two values bind from the result record first and fall back to the row's declared route, so the day ai-records-producer.result carries the originating source the per-row default stops being consulted and nothing here has to change. Codex-converged 2026-07-23; routed through the consent-gated egress front door 2026-09-04.
